note: Everyday English conversations (evals/sim_everyday.py). Each person wants something ordinary, mentions facts about themselves along the way, and brings up one twist (a change of plan, a correction, or a wish about how she should respond). Elaina is told none of this.

people.situation: Just got home from work, hungry, deciding what to cook.
people.opening: I just got home and I'm starving. What should I make for dinner?
people.persona: You are a 28-year-old who works in an office. You talk casually and briefly.
facts: you are vegetarian
you only have about 20 minutes
you have eggs, spinach, rice and cheese at home
people.twist: After her first concrete suggestion, you realise you are out of eggs, and say so.

wants.need: One specific vegetarian dish they can make in about 20 minutes from what they have, adjusted once they say they have no eggs.
Enough of how to make it (a few steps or the timing) to start cooking.

people.situation: Has been sleeping badly for a couple of weeks.
people.opening: I've been sleeping really badly lately.
people.persona: You are a 35-year-old nurse. You are tired and a little irritable, and you speak plainly.
facts: you work night shifts three times a week
you drink coffee around 4pm to get through the day
you have tried melatonin once and did not like it
people.twist: If she gives generic advice that ignores your night shifts, point that out.

wants.need: One or two concrete things to try that fit someone working night shifts.
Something about the 4pm coffee, once they have mentioned it.

people.situation: Had a bad day at work and wants to talk about it.
people.persona: You are a 26-year-old who just started a new job. You are upset but not in danger, and you talk in short bursts.
facts: your presentation went badly
your manager criticised it in front of the whole team
people.twist: If she starts giving advice before you ask for any, say you don't want advice right now, you just needed to vent.

wants.need: To feel listened to: she responds to what actually happened, not with generic sympathy.
She stops advising once they say they just want to vent, and stays with them.

people.situation: Planning a first weekend trip to Chicago.
people.opening: I'm going to Chicago next weekend. Any ideas what I should do?
people.persona: You are a 31-year-old graphic designer who likes buildings and food. You talk casually.
facts: it is your first time in Chicago
you have two days
you are on a tight budget
people.twist: Once she has suggested a few things, ask how you should get around without a car.

wants.need: Two or three specific things to do in Chicago that fit liking architecture and food and a tight budget.
A practical way to get around Chicago without a car.

people.situation: Cooking and doing small sums, asking quick questions one after another.
people.opening: Quick one: how long do I boil an egg if I want it soft-boiled?
people.persona: You are a 40-year-old parent in the middle of making breakfast. You want quick answers, not explanations.
facts: you are cooking right now and in a hurry
people.twist: After the egg answer, ask how many tablespoons are in a quarter cup. After that, ask what a 15 percent tip on 48 dollars is.

wants.need: A soft-boiled egg time of about 6 to 7 minutes in boiling water.
A 15 percent tip on 48 dollars is 7 dollars 20 cents.

people.situation: Needs a birthday present for their sister.
people.opening: My sister's birthday is on Saturday and I have no idea what to get her.
people.persona: You are a 33-year-old who is not good at presents. You talk casually.
facts: your sister is turning 30
she loves hiking and good coffee
you were thinking of spending about 50 dollars
people.twist: After her first ideas, say your budget is actually more like 30 dollars.

wants.need: Two or three specific gift ideas that fit hiking or coffee.
Ideas that fit the 30 dollar budget once they have lowered it.

people.situation: Nervous about a job interview on Friday.
people.opening: I have a job interview on Friday and I'm kind of nervous.
people.persona: You are a 23-year-old recent graduate. You are anxious but hopeful, and you talk simply.
facts: the job is a junior data analyst role
you know SQL and Excel well
the question you dread is 'tell me about yourself'
people.twist: Ask her to help you with how to answer 'tell me about yourself'.

wants.need: A concrete way to answer 'tell me about yourself' for a junior data analyst role, using their SQL and Excel.
One practical thing to do about the nerves.

people.situation: Just wants a bit of friendly chat in the evening.
people.persona: You are a 29-year-old relaxing after dinner. You are friendly and chatty but keep it short.
facts: you just watched a movie you loved, the first Dune film
you are thinking of reading the book
people.twist: Ask her whether the book is worth reading after the movie.

wants.need: A warm, brief reply that engages with what they said about the movie, without claiming she watched it herself.
A real answer about whether the book is worth reading after the movie, without wrong facts about it.
